question: A team is redesigning a multi-day customer-support assistant that currently relies only on rolling summarization of the transcript and unfiltered tool outputs, and has been losing exact figures, mixing up simultaneous issues, and missing details from lengthy middle sections of aggregated reports. Which combination of changes would most directly address all of these failure modes together?
options: A) Switch to the model with the largest context window and stop summarizing at all, while keeping the current tool-output and aggregation structure unchanged
B) Summarize the transcript more frequently, keep all raw tool output for completeness, and add a closing reminder to double-check earlier sections
C) Maintain a case-facts block, keep separate records per active issue, trim tool outputs to relevant fields, and lead aggregated input with headed key findings
D) Ask customers to restate key details periodically, forward full subagent reasoning chains unchanged, and rely on default handling of long documents
correct_answers: C) Maintain a case-facts block, keep separate records per active issue, trim tool outputs to relevant fields, and lead aggregated input with headed key findings
explanations: A larger context window may delay when limits are hit but does not fix unfiltered tool-output bloat, blended multi-issue narratives, or the placement of key findings within a document.

More frequent summarization still compresses figures each time, keeping all raw tool output reintroduces the token-bloat problem, and a closing reminder does not restructure content to fix position effects.

Correct — each element (persistent case facts, per-issue structured records, trimmed tool outputs, and up-front findings with headers) targets one of the specific failure modes described, and together they address numeric loss, issue mixing, token bloat, and middle-of-document omissions.

Relying on customers to restate details burdens users rather than fixing the system, and forwarding unfiltered subagent reasoning reintroduces the exact token-budget problem structured outputs are meant to solve.
